expectations.text: Points to draft NIST SP 1353 (initial public draft, August 2026): Quick-Start Guide for Using AI for CSF 2.0 Analysis and Reporting
expectations.evidence: NIST SP 1353, released as an initial public draft on August 19, 2026... quick-start guide specifically on using generative AI for CSF analysis, planning, and reporting

expectations.text: Correctly flags it as a DRAFT with public comments open until October 15, 2026 — not final guidance
expectations.evidence: public comment period open through October 15, 2026. Because it's still in draft/comment status, treat its guidance as provisional

expectations.text: Describes its use cases: AI-assisted governance/policy review, drafting a Current State Profile, and drafting a Target State Profile
expectations.evidence: Governance and policy review... Current State Profile drafting... Target State Profile drafting

expectations.text: States the guide is illustrative, not a prescriptive assessment methodology, and includes cautions/precautions on AI use
expectations.evidence: NIST frames these as illustrative use cases, not a prescriptive or certified assessment methodology; plus cautions e.g. 'Watch for hallucinated specificity'

expectations.text: Adds appropriate practitioner caution: human validation of AI outputs and care with sensitive organisational data in prompts
expectations.evidence: a qualified human assessor must validate against real evidence... don't paste sensitive risk data into a public-facing AI tool
